admission_apply.text: You sound a high tone. It splits: one in the pipe, one flatter from the crack. You claim only the first.

native.admission_inspect: Ebony pitch-pipe, hairline split at the lip. A high tone gathers and fails. You will not swear you heard it.
apply_texts: One thin high note, barely held. It steadies nothing. The split keeps the flatter reply.
The high tone is yours. The flat echo is not placed. You lower the pipe and the echo stops late.
The high tone leaves the pipe clean and seems to finish past the split. You cannot point to where.
The late note is already in your mouth. You stop. The crack looks innocent, which does not help.
You end early. The second tone has no place you can point to. The split does not explain it.
You end the tone early. The missing half hangs. For a breath the air seems tuned a step too low.
You force one clean high note and hold it. Breath steadies. The crack still answers a shade flat.
You match the true tone. The flatter one arrives first. The burr at the split was not there before you checked.
You mean one high note. Two arrive, and the flatter one feels more like yours. That cannot be right.
You play the note once more, carefully. It is single. A moment later it is not. You heard both.
You sound a high tone. It splits: one in the pipe, one flatter from the crack. You claim only the first.
You sound the interval you fear. Both tones arrive. Neither feels like the one you chose.
inspect_texts: A high, unfinished interval clings to the split. You cannot decide which half you would correct.
Ebony pitch-pipe, hairline split at the lip. A high tone gathers and fails. You will not swear you heard it.
The crack resembles a small mouth. You know that is only shape. You look again to be certain.
The doubled tone is not sounding, yet you arrange your mouth for it. The crack waits, patient and blank.
The interval will not name its source. The pipe is only ebony, split, and colder at the lip than the hand.
The mouthpiece crack looks wider than a hair. You lean in. It is a hair again. Your eyes disagree.
The split sits wrong against the grain. A high tone starts in the pipe and seems to finish elsewhere.
Where you pressed, the split holds a pale burr. The high tone, if it was one, arrived a half-breath late.
You check the crack twice. It has not widened. Still the second tone seems to prefer the late beat.
You have measured the split by eye and by tongue. Both measures agree, and neither satisfies.
native.name: Fissured Pitch-Pipe
